title: [22/03/2023] - Two Processes of Black Tea Production
prompt: The diagram below shows two different processes for manufacturing black tea. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates two distinct manufacturing processes used to produce black tea, comparing traditional methods for making loose tea with modern techniques for creating tea bags.

frame.name: Overall
paragraphs: Overall, both processes share identical initial and final stages, with the main differences occurring in the middle processing steps. While the traditional method involves rolling leaves to create loose tea, the modern approach uses cutting techniques to produce smaller granular pieces suitable for tea bags.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The manufacturing process begins identically for both methods. First, only the bud and top leaves are carefully picked from tea plants to ensure good quality. These fresh leaves then undergo withering, where air is passed through them on racks, removing 60% of their moisture content.The processes diverge significantly in the next stage. In the traditional method, the withered leaves are rolled flat and broken, releasing enzymes from the leaves. Conversely, the modern method involves cutting, tearing and curling the leaves, which creates quick-processing smaller granular pieces rather than whole leaves.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Both methods then follow identical final steps. The processed leaves undergo oxidation and fermentation, during which they are spread on tiles or cement surfaces. This stage causes the leaves to change to a copper color as enzymes react with air, developing flavor and aroma. Finally, the leaves are dried until 97% of moisture is removed, completing the black tea manufacturing process.
